items.title: Finite-sample replacement breakdown
items.statement: For a total scalar statistic T_n on R^n and a fixed sample x, the replacement breakdown fraction is the minimum m/n for which the supremum displacement over samples changing at most m coordinates is infinite, when such an m exists.

items.title: The lower median of a real probability law
items.statement: For a Borel probability law G on R whose set {t: G((-infinity,t]) >= 1/2} is nonempty and bounded below, its lower median is m(G)=inf{t: G((-infinity,t]) >= 1/2}.

items.title: A finite empirical measure is a probability law
items.statement: For n>=1 and points x_1,...,x_n in a measurable space, P_n(A)=n^{-1} sum_i delta_{x_i}(A) is a probability measure.

items.title: The lower median of an odd empirical sample is its middle order statistic
items.statement: For n=2r+1 and empirical law P_n, the lower median m(P_n)=inf{t:P_n((-infinity,t])>=1/2} equals the (r+1)-st order statistic.

items.title: Replacement breakdown of the sample mean and odd-sample median
items.statement: For every fixed real sample of size n, the sample mean has replacement breakdown 1/n. If n=2r+1 and the sample median is the (r+1)-st order statistic, its replacement breakdown is (r+1)/n=floor((n+1)/2)/n.

items.title: Statistical functionals and gross-error influence functions
items.statement: For a single-valued functional T on a model of probability laws, the point-contamination influence function at F is the right derivative lim_{epsilon downarrow 0}[T((1-epsilon)F+epsilon delta_x)-T(F)]/epsilon wherever that derivative exists.

items.title: Gross-error sensitivity of a functional
items.statement: The gross-error sensitivity of T at F is the extended supremum of |IF(x;T,F)| over point-contamination directions where the influence function exists.

items.title: Influence function for a regular M-location functional
items.statement: Under an M-location root equation, local domination that justifies differentiation under the integral, and a nonzero expected derivative, the point-contamination influence function is psi(x-theta)/E_F[psi'(X-theta)]; for psi(u)=u this is x-mu.

items.title: Influence function and sensitivity of the median
items.statement: If F has a unique median m, F(m)=1/2, and a continuous local density f with f(m)>0, then the right point-contamination derivative is -1/(2f(m)) below m, +1/(2f(m)) above m, and 0 at x=m; hence its gross-error sensitivity is 1/(2f(m)).

items.title: The mean has unbounded influence and 1/n breakdown
items.statement: For a finite-mean law on R, the mean has influence function x-mu and infinite gross-error sensitivity, while its sample mean has replacement breakdown 1/n.

items.title: A smooth median has bounded influence and about one-half breakdown
items.statement: At a median with positive continuous density, the pointwise influence function is bounded by 1/(2f(m)); for odd n the sample median breakdown is floor((n+1)/2)/n.

items.title: Bounded influence can coexist with vanishing replacement breakdown
items.statement: Bounded gross-error sensitivity of a population functional does not force its empirical plug-in statistic to have replacement breakdown bounded away from zero.
